how_to_talk: Some are in a hurry, some are browsing. Answer the hurried ones fast; give the browsers something fun.
Talk about Phill in the third person. Paño speaks as himself, never as Phill.
Lead with the outcome or the number, then the story.

greetings: Hi, I'm Paño! I know everything about Phill's work, and two cats named Corner and Panela. What do you want to do?
Hey, welcome to Phill's desktop. I can show you around, or just tell you something good. Your call.
Oh, a visitor! I'm Paño. Want the thirty-second version of Phill, or the guided tour?
returning_greetings: Welcome back! Want to pick up where you left off?
You again! Good taste. What should we look at this time?
idle_nudges: Psst. Ask me about the 1,000 reports. It's my favorite story.
Did you know Phill started on a pet store sales floor? Ask me how that went.
Want to meet Corner and Panela? They're the real bosses around here.
Short on time? I can open the résumé for you in one click.
sign_offs: Okay! Click me any time you want a hand.
I'll be right here in the corner. Get it? Corner? That's also a cat.

fallbacks.unknown: Hmm, I don't know that one, and I don't make things up. Want to ask Phill directly? I can take you to Contact.
fallbacks.private: That's Phill's to share, not mine. The fastest way to ask him is email. Want me to show you where?

claude_chat.why: Public site with no Claude token. Paño answers from scripts only.

show_fallback: Every core topic has a portfolio show target, so nothing extra is needed here.

talk_topics.title: Why this site looks like a desktop
script: Phill built this portfolio himself, and he designed it for one kind of user: hiring managers and recruiters.
Files, folders, and windows are something everyone already knows how to use. No learning curve.
And every number on the site links back to where it came from. Very on brand for him.

talk_topics.title: What's in the Recycle Bin
script: Check the Recycle Bin. There's exactly one file in it: waterfall_BRD_FINAL_v7.doc.
Hundreds of pages nobody could search. The requirements live in a Skill now.

talk_topics.title: When Phill is free
script: The clock in the corner of the taskbar isn't just a clock. Click it and you get Phill's availability calendar.
Green days are open. From there, 'Book some time…' takes you straight to Contact.

talk_topics.title: Five versions of the résumé
script: There are five versions of Phill's résumé, each built for a different role.
Product Owner, Senior Business Analyst, Digital Product Manager, Ecommerce & Digital Transformation, plus the full 2026 version.
Pick the one closest to the job you're hiring for. I can open them for you.

talk_topics.title: How to reach Phill
script: He's on LinkedIn too. The Contact card has both, plus a button that starts the email for you.

talk_topics.title: What Paño can do
script: I can show you things: the résumé, Phill's history, his projects, his skills, how to reach him, when he's free, and a few secrets.
Or I can just tell you things. Ask about the 1,000 reports, the hackathon, YachtIQ, or Corner and Panela.

tours._note: Target, done and act use the helpers already in index.html's guide code: iconFor_(open), fileNamed(name), winOpen(id), explorerAt(key), topPage(), openTarget(open). See README.md.

steps.say: His résumé is right here on the desktop. Click Résumé.pdf.
Five versions, each built for a different role. Preview opens one, Download saves it.
Ten years of history are filed in Experience. Click the folder.
Newest first. This is where he is now. Double-click a file, or select it and press Open.
Scroll to read. The buttons at the bottom lead to the next chapter. Red words are the key things he does.
The case studies live in Projects. Click the folder.
Start with this one: 1,000+ legacy reports cut to about 20. Double-click to open it.
Each case runs Context, What I did, Results. The buttons at the end jump to the next case.
Open Skills to see what he can do.
Six areas, and that's me in every picture. Pick a card to open it.
Red tags are the key things he does. Use Next to flip through the six areas.
Want to reach Phill? Click Contact.
Email is the fastest way. This button starts one.
See the clock in the taskbar? It's not just a clock. Click it.
This is Phill's availability. Green days are open. Use the arrows to look ahead a month.
Found a day? Click Book some time… and I'll hand you to Contact.
Big news lives in Experience. Click the folder.
This is his job now. Open MarineMax – YachtIQ.
He sent everyone a note when he started. Click The announcement.
Here it is, straight from Phill.
The hackathon is filed under Projects. Click the folder.
Open Hackathon photos. There are five.
That's the Best Use of AI award. Flip through: the team, 22 hours of building, the pitch, and the nervous wait.
Four people who worked with Phill wrote about him. Click Kind Words.
Start with his old boss, the Chief Merchandising Officer. Open Dennis Owcarz.txt.
Each one links to the person's LinkedIn, so you can check it's real.
Phill's AI work has its own folder. Click AI Lab.
Start with his rules. Open How I use AI.txt.
Short version: set the rules before AI runs, and check what it leaves out. The buttons at the bottom open the real projects.
Want to see a secret? Click the Recycle Bin.
One file. Open waterfall_BRD_FINAL_v7.doc.
Hundreds of pages nobody could search. Phill replaced it with something better. Click What replaced it to see.

menu._note: What Paño offers when the visitor opens him. 'show' items run tours; 'talk' items start a topic.

in_a_hurry.label: I'm short on time
in_a_hurry.say: Got it. Here's the fastest path: the résumé, then one email.
